content.title: About
content.content: Gravy made with soy sauce is a thick, aromatic sauce created by reducing broth, soy sauce, sugar, and spices. The recipe was first recorded in 1921 and has since become a versatile condiment for meats, potatoes, and rice.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial soy‑sauce gravy recipe appeared in the United States in 1921.
Soy sauce gives the gravy a distinctive umami flavor and dark color.
Gravy is often used in fusion cuisine, blending Eastern and Western traditions.
To achieve a thicker consistency, starch or flour is sometimes added.
Vegetarian versions replace meat broth with mushroom or vegetable stock.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Soy sauce provides plant‑based protein that can boost the nutritional profile of the dish.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Fermented products like soy sauce contain antioxidants that help protect cells.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fermentation improves the bioavailability of certain nutrients.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: When sugar is used sparingly, the gravy remains relatively low‑calorie.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Soy sauce is a good source of iron, magnesium, and potassium, important for metabolism.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Soy sauce is salty, so people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to soy products.

items.title: Glutamate content
items.content: The gravy may contain added monosodium glutamate, which can cause headaches in sensitive people.

items.title: Calorie increase with sugar
items.content: Excessive sugar raises the calorie count of the sauce.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot soy‑sauce gravy over roasted meat, chicken, fish, mashed potatoes, rice, or vegetables. It can also be used as a base for braising or as a dipping sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared gravy in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions; bring to a boil before serving.
